title: NeurOCNN: A Neural-Operator-Based Model for Physiological Time Series
claim: A staged architecture turns variable-rate input signals into fixed-size features via continuous convolutions and basis pooling, then into predictions.
layout: Two rows of dashed module boxes, snaking left-to-right then right-to-left, with arrows
description: A two-row architecture diagram with arrows between pastel dashed-outline module boxes. The top row starts with a Physiological Signal, shown as stacked waveforms with C, N and a legend. It feeds a purple Spline Convolution 1D box, which shows stacked kernel blocks, a convolution symbol, a spline curve with control points and sampling points, and a 'Sample' arrow. GELU and Group Norm blocks follow, with a loop arrow labeled N' that repeats the convolution block. Next is a red Fourier Basis Pooling box with the signal, real Fourier basis waveforms and the formula c_{b,m} = Σ φ_m(t̃_n) Δt_n Z_{b,n}. It outputs constant-size features. An arrow drops to the bottom row: Transformer with Pre-Norm, then an orange Attention Pooling box (MHA with Q, K and V stacks and a learnable query), then a green Output box with a classification head producing ŷ. Orange and green arrows show the flow, and the eye goes first to the colorful Spline Convolution box.

abstract: Neural operators have become a central tool in scientific machine learning for learning discretization-consistent solution operators, achieving strong results on partial differential equation (PDE) benchmarks. Physiological time series, however, are highly nonstationary and dominated by localized transient events, properties that can challenge both PDE-oriented neural operators and conventional deep models. We propose NeurOCNN, a neural-operator-based model for physiological signals that learns a robust function-to-label mapping. NeurOCNN integrates continuous-time, spline-parameterized convolutions to capture localized morphology with Fourier projection pooling for variable-to-fixed dimensional mapping, thereby enabling robust, discretization-invariant inference under zero-shot sampling-rate shifts. Empirically, NeurOCNN outperforms standard neural-operator baselines, achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods, and maintains stable accuracy across multiple previously unseen evaluation sampling rates. The code is available at https://github.com/Idsl-group/NeurOCNN.
